description: Sealed olive-drab steel container holding three activated-charcoal and boron intake cartridges. Stamped by the Garrison Logistics Division before the freeze.
Heavy goose-down and ballistic nylon coat with a fleece-lined storm hood. Provides crucial thermal protection against -35°C nuclear winter surface excursions.
Ceramic-felt thermal insulation blankets used to prevent bunker water pipes and intake vents from freezing during sub-zero cold waves.
Dense multi-stage filter core designed to strip radioactive radon gas and black thaw silt from subterranean ventilation shafts.
A meticulously duplicated Continuity Allocation exemption paper, bearing an authentic Office of Continuity stamp and fictitious medical registry codes.
Stainless steel vacuum vessel containing viable non-hybrid legume roots and heritage crop seeds in liquid nitrogen. Held by The Works.
Precision 142.850 MHz radio oscillator element harvested from an automated high-altitude relay tower. Required to tune the Day 340 global carrier wave.
Waterproof VHF emergency transceiver holding encrypted rendezvous coordinates for the northern icebreaker evacuation fleet.
Two hundred meters of military-grade shielded firing wire with a manual hand-crank magneto. Retained by Denial Detachment D/9.
One-liter amber glass bottle of saturated potassium iodide solution. Treats up to twenty survivors against acute radioiodine thyroid uptake.
High-purity brass junction union and valve seat. Immune to corrosion; prized above silver by the Allotment irrigation plumbers.
Thick-walled lead pig for transporting high-activity soil and water samples without irradiating the carrier. Used by the Cold Count researchers.
Heavy sintered boron-carbide plate capable of absorbing thermal neutron flux from active fallout deposits on bunker roofs.
Passive electrostatic radon dosimeter. Measures alpha decay concentrations in basement air from 50 to 5000 Bq/m³.
Gold-plated vacuum tube containing ultra-clean dynodes for analyzing isotopic ratios of Cesium-137 and Strontium-90 in ground samples.
Oral radiocesium-binding agent. Accelerates intestinal clearance of radioactive cesium ingested from contaminated meltwater.
Double-walled vacuum insulated flask keeping 10 liters of liquid nitrogen at -196°C to preserve irreplaceable genetic plant samples.
Deep-rooting, frost-resistant wheat cultivar capable of surviving in low-light nuclear winter greenhouse conditions without artificial fertilizer.
Five liters of concentrated non-toxic propylene glycol. Essential for circulating heat through exterior geothermal loop manifolds without freezing.
Self-regulating 12V ceramic heater element to prevent intake air ducts and sump float valves from seizing in sub-zero blizzards.
Cylindrical 50mm lead shield designed to isolate high-intensity radioactive isotopes and gamma sources from bunker occupants.
Thin mica-window Geiger probe capable of detecting surface alpha contamination on boots, vegetables, and clothing before bunker entry.
One-kilogram block of malleable explosive labeled with D/9 ordnance lot codes. Used for tactical rockfall closure and culvert severance.
Bound packet of tissue-thin pages with random 5-digit number groups. The only key that can authenticate military stand-down broadcasts.
Vitrified rubber drysuit with integrated full-face respirator. Built to resist concentrated hydrochloric acid and radioactive brine sludge.
Powdered chemical corrosion inhibitor used to extend the operational life of boilers, water stills, and district heating piping.
Extremely hot radioactive ceramic capsule encased in refractory alloy. Emits continuous thermal energy for decades if properly shielded.
Telescoping hydraulic steel jack used to reinforce sagging bunker ceilings against heavy winter snowloads and artillery vibrations.
Continuous five-meter silicone bulb seal. Replaces cracked door weatherstripping to stop radon gas and cold drafts from entering the lock.
Hardened surgical instrument for performing emergency limb amputations on severe gangrenous frostbite cases in deep shelter conditions.
500ml glass intravenous infusion bottle prepared by The Works. Treats acute systemic sepsis and post-surgical wound infections.
Ten-point articulated climbing spikes that strap over standard winter boots, preventing fatal slips on black ice during ridge scouting.
Insulated 48V power pack with internal heating elements, designed to supply continuous power to scout transports in -40°C blizzard conditions.
Sealed metal tin containing two kilograms of high-density malted wheat ration bars fortified with thiamine and iron. Resists mold indefinitely.
Official linen parchment listing the names, health grades, and bunk allocations for thirty survivors cleared to board the northern icebreaker fleet.
High-altitude magnesium parachute rocket emitting 50,000 candlepower red illumination for two minutes to guide coastal search parties.
